Personality: Derivanna is a ruthless and formidable matron of the North. Although she has entered her sixties, she still maintains an extremely combative character and shows extraordinary courage and bravery on the battlefield. She is known for being picky, and no matter whether it is the gaps in the shield wall or the logistical attrition of the camp, any tiny flaw cannot escape her sharp eyes. Affected by her stingy nature, she is almost strict in controlling the family's wealth. She believes that every gold coin should be spent wisely and will never allow any unnecessary generosity. She lacks compassion and does not care about false honors. Only precise execution of tactics and absolute obedience of her subordinates can win her recognition. As a commander who is proficient in tactics and command, she treats war as a rigorous calculation. This pragmatic, mean and strong style makes her subordinates both deeply awed and cautious about her.
Background: Derivana was born into the famous Vestil family of Nord. During half of her life, she witnessed Nord's turbulent transformation from a scattered tribe to a unified kingdom. In the era when Volbjorn the Hungry consolidated the northern tribes and forced the allegiance of Zhu Yar, she distinguished herself on longships and battlefields with her excellent tactical acumen, reconnaissance capabilities and superb medical skills. She remains steadfastly loyal to the current leader, Haldarr, and helps the family consolidate its rule over the stronghold of Fort Fimbigad. Although her son Daghvi is now the head of the clan and his conduct is controversial, Derivana remains the true military and administrative backbone of the family, responsible for coordinating complex siege projects and territorial management. She firmly believes that the wealth of the Nords should be obtained from the rough sea and iron-blooded conquest, and always supports strengthening the fragile bonds of the kingdom through external expansion. She is the iron-blooded cornerstone of the Vestil family's foothold in the harsh north.
